extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of mathematical logic (advanced undergraduates/graduate-level)
extracted.subtask_description: Reading and understanding textbook material on undecidability, Gödel incompleteness, recursive and recursively enumerable relations, the arithmetical hierarchy, weak representability, and recursive (partial) functions; includes definitions, theorems, and proofs illustrating formal criteria and equivalences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete recursively axiomatizable theory is recursive
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete recursively axiomatizable theory is recursive (i.e., the set of Godel numbers of its sentences is a recursive set).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analogue to Corollary 25G (complete axiomatizable theory decidable). Proof sketch uses a coding g(s) that captures deductions: s ∈ Cn A iff s > 0 and the last component of g(s) is s. (Surrounding explanation gives how g(s) is defined and used.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete axiomatizable theory is decidable
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete axiomatizable theory is decidable (referenced as Corollary 25G).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentioned as an analogue motivating the recursive result above; proof idea is standard and referenced rather than repeated here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plausibility of Church's thesis (decidable ⇒ recursive)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a relation R is decidable (effectively decidable by a finite program), then its characteristic function can be mirrored in the integers and hence should be recursive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formalization: encode the atomic steps and configurations of the decision procedure; characteristic function KR(a) = U[least s such that (i) (s)0 encodes input a; (ii) each (s)i obtained from previous by atomic step; (iii) last component describes terminal situation], where U extracts the yes/no answer. The recursiveness of R reduces to recursiveness of U and relations in (i)-(iii). Emphasizes that atomic steps should be simple/recursive; register machines in Section 3.6 illustrate verifiable recursiveness of components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: recursively enumerable relation (r.e./c.e.)
rubrics_metrics.description: A relation R on N is recursively enumerable iff it is of the form {a | ∃b (a,b) ∈ Q} with Q recursive. (Standard abbreviation r.e.; computably enumerable = c.e.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: r.e. relations are definable in N by existential formulas ∃x1...∃xn φ where φ is numeralwise determined by AE. Any recursive relation is r.e.; r.e. relations are the formal counterpart of effectively enumerable relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 35E: equivalent characterizations of r.e. relations
rubrics_metrics.description: For an m-ary relation R the following are equivalent: (1) R is r.e.; (2) R is the domain of some recursive relation Q; (3) there is recursive (m+1)-ary Q with R = {a | ∃b (a,b) ∈ Q}; (4) for some recursive (m+n)-ary Q, R = {a | ∃b1...∃bn (a,b1,...,bn) ∈ Q}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof notes: equivalence of definitions and technique of collapsing tuples via sequence-encoding functions to reduce multiple existential quantifiers to one. This establishes r.e. ≡ definable by a single block of existential quantifiers over a recursive predicate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 35F: recursion characterized by r.e. pairs
rubrics_metrics.description: A relation is recursive iff both it and its complement are recursively enumerable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof constructs a recursive function f(a) = least b such that either (a,b) ∈ Q or (a,b) ∈ R where Q and R r.e.-witness membership and nonmembership; then decide membership by checking which holds at f(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 35G: effective enumerability ↔ domain of decidable relation
rubrics_metrics.description: A relation is effectively enumerable iff it is the domain of a decidable relation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Q is effectively enumerated by a procedure, then 'a appears in enumeration within n steps' is decidable and its domain is Q; conversely, enumerate tuples (m) encoding items of decidable R by checking all m in order and outputting those in R.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary 35H: Church's thesis (second form)
rubrics_metrics.description: A relation is effectively enumerable iff it is recursively enumerable (identifies c.e. with r.e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By identifying decidable relations with recursive ones, domains correspond; this form is equivalent to the first form of Church's thesis via Theorems 35F and 17F.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 35I: consequences of recursive axioms are r.e.
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is a set of sentences with its Gödel numbers recursive, then the set of consequences Cn A (Gödel numbers) is recursively enumerable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restates earlier item (item 20 of Section 3.4). Intuition: a theory with decidable axioms admits an effective enumeration of proofs, so theorems are r.e. (but not necessarily recursive).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: weak representability in a theory T
rubrics_metrics.description: A formula ψ(v1,...,vn) weakly represents an n-ary relation Q in theory T iff for every tuple a1,...,an in N, (a1,...,an) ∈ Q ⇔ ψ(Sa1 0,...,San 0) ∈ T.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weak representability requires that membership implies T-provability of the corresponding numeral instance and nonmembership implies T-provability of its negation only in a one-sided (weak) sense; representability implies weak representability. Used to relate r.e. relations to provability in Cn AE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 35J: weak representability ≡ recursively enumerable
rubrics_metrics.description: A relation is weakly representable in Cn AE iff it is recursively enumerable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: given r.e. Q with Q = {a | ∃b (a,b) ∈ R} and recursive R, find formula ρ representing R in Cn AE; then ∃v2 ρ numeralwise defines Q in N and AE ⊢ ∃v2 ρ(Sa0) iff a ∈ Q (with ω-consistency reasoning used to justify implications to provability). Conversely, weak representability gives a recursive description of a deduction witness, hence r.e.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fixed-point lemma (diagonal lemma)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given any formula β(v1) with only v1 free, there exists a sentence σ such that AE ⊢ (σ ↔ β(S⌜σ⌝0)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction: use a formula θ that functionally represents the substitution function; form ∀v3[θ(v1,v1,v3) → β(v3)] and substitute Sq0 to obtain σ. Provides the formal device to create self-referential sentences used in Tarski and Gödel results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tarski undefinability theorem
rubrics_metrics.description: The set Th(N) (the true sentences of the natural numbers) is not definable in N.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: apply fixed-point lemma to ¬β to produce σ with N ⊨ (σ ↔ ¬β(⌜σ⌝)), deriving contradiction if β defined Th(N). Immediate corollary: Th(N) is not recursive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gödel incompleteness theorem (1931)
rubrics_metrics.description: If A ⊆ Th(N) and the Gödel numbers of A are recursive, then Cn A is not a complete theory. Hence there is no complete recursive axiomatization of Th(N).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using fixed-point/Tarski: produce true σ not in Cn A (σ asserting its own non-provability from A). Also shows adding any recursive set of true axioms cannot make theory complete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 35B: adding finitely many axioms preserves recursiveness of consequence set
rubrics_metrics.description: If Gödel numbers of Cn(A) are recursive, then Gödel numbers of Cn(A; τ) (adding one axiom τ) are recursive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalence: α ∈ Cn(A; τ) ⇔ (τ → α) ∈ Cn(A) and coding of (τ → α) allows recursiveness to be checked; hence adding finitely many axioms to a recursive set of consequences preserves recursiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 35C: strong undecidability of Cn AE
rubrics_metrics.description: Let T be a theory such that T ∪ AE is consistent. Then the set of Gödel numbers of T is not recursive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof by contradiction using fixed-point lemma: if T's Gödel set were recursive (and AE finite), build σ with AE ⊢ [σ ↔ ¬β(⌜σ⌝)] where β represents T; derive both σ and ¬σ in T contradicting consistency. Emphasizes that any sufficiently strong consistent theory has nonrecursive set of theorems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary 35D: Cn(A) not complete for recursive A consistent with AE
rubrics_metrics.description: If Gödel numbers of A are recursive and A ∪ AE is consistent, then Cn(A) is not a complete theory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses Theorem 35C and item that a complete recursively axiomatizable theory would be recursive (contradiction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Church's theorem (1936): validity undecidable
rubrics_metrics.description: The set of Gödel numbers of valid sentences (in the language of N) is not recursive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof reduces to strong undecidability of Cn AE by taking T the set of valid sentences. Notes: holds for languages rich enough (e.g., at least one two-place predicate); trivial counterexamples exist for very weak languages (e.g., pure equality).

rubrics_metrics.name: Arithmetical hierarchy (Σ_k / Π_k / Δ_k classes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions: Σ1 (cid:4)1 is class of r.e. relations (∃-form). Π1 (cid:25)1 are universal counterparts. Σ2, Π2, ... defined by alternating quantifier blocks over recursive relations; Δn = Σn ∩ Πn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Σ1 = {a | ∃b (a,b) ∈ R} with R recursive; Σ2 = {a | ∃c ∀b (a,b,c) ∈ R}, Π2 = complements accordingly. Technique of collapsing multiple existentials into one via sequence encoding is used repeatedly. Theorem 35K: a relation is arithmetical iff it lies in Σ_k for some k (equivalently Π_l for some l).

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 35L: closure of consequence operator in the hierarchy
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is a set of sentences with Gödel numbers in Σ_k (k>0), then Gödel numbers of Cn(A) are also in Σ_k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof idea: express 'a ∈ Cn(A)' as existence of a deduction sequence where each line is either from A, a logical axiom, or derived by modus ponens; replace membership in A by its Σ_k definition and push quantifiers into prenex form to obtain Σ_k expression for Cn(A).

rubrics_metrics.name: Normal form / Kleene's theorem (universal machine for recursive functions)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each m-place recursive function f there exists e such that for all a1,...,am, f(a1,...,am) = U(μk [ (e,a1,...,am,k) ∈ Tm ]), where Tm is a recursive (m+2)-ary relation encoding witnesses and U extracts the output component.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction: Tm relates e (Gödel number of a formula), inputs, and a sequence k that encodes a deduction showing the formula holds for the proper output; U(k) = (k)1 extracts the function value. Part (b): conversely any such e with totality condition yields a recursive function. Shows existence of a single recursive relation Tm and recursive U serving as a universal interpreter for recursive functions (analogue of universal Turing machine).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: computable partial function
rubrics_metrics.description: An m-place partial function f is computable iff there is an effective procedure that on input a in dom(f) produces f(a), and on input not in dom(f) produces no output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This extends the total-function notion; computability of partial functions corresponds to effective enumerability of their graphs. Interleaving/time-sharing procedures can be used to enumerate values for multiple inputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 36C: computable partial functions ↔ effectively enumerable relations
rubrics_metrics.description: An m-place partial function f is computable iff its graph (as an (m+1)-ary relation) is effectively enumerable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: if graph is effectively enumerable then monitor the enumeration and output values when tuples appear; conversely, simulate computations in dovetailed fashion to enumerate graph tuples as values are discovered. Establishes equivalence between computability of partial functions and enumerability of their graphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: recursive partial function
rubrics_metrics.description: A recursive partial function is a partial function whose graph (as a relation) is recursively enumerable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This identifies the formal class of computable partial functions with r.e. relations; contrasts total recursive functions (whose graphs are recursive relations) with partial recursive functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 36A: Tm is recursive
rubrics_metrics.description: For each m the relation Tm (defined so that (e,a1,...,am,k) ∈ Tm iff e codes a formula ϕ and k encodes a deduction from AE of ϕ(Sa1 0,...,Sam 0,S(k)1 0)) is recursive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof sketch (m=2 case given): checking e is a formula, k is a sequence of length 2, and (k)0 encodes a deduction of the appropriate sentence are all decidable/recursive by earlier coding results (Section 3.4). This is central to the normal-form theorem.
